title: RUN!
summary: Reassess the mating threat after a pawn disappears, then sacrifice a queen to gain time for connected passers.

nodes.question: Which pawn move changes the rook’s checking options?
nodes.explanation: White has Kg1 and c3/c4/d6/h6 against Kh3/Rf5. Offering the forward c-pawn prepares a supported advance rather than immediately pushing a promotion pawn.

nodes.question: Why can White promote now but not earlier?
nodes.explanation: This separately reviewed source diagram is after the return to Kg1/...Kg3, once Black has captured c3. With c3 gone, a queen on h8 can guard a1 along the diagonal.

branches.title: Start the pawn chain and draw the king toward c3
commentary: Begin in the complete seven-piece source root. The king walk follows the illustrated mating-threat mechanism.
c5 offers the forward c-pawn and changes the rook’s defensive options. The selected ...Kg3 continuation declines the offer.
Kg3 cuts off White’s king along the second rank.
h7 threatens promotion before the rook can take on c5.
Rf8 returns to the back rank and stops h8 promotion for now.
c6 prepares the connected passers by guarding d7, where the d-pawn wants to advance.
Ra8 creates a threat of ...Ra1 mate while the white king is confined.
Kf1 steps away from that immediate mating pattern.
Kf3 renews the mating threat with the king opposite White’s king.
Ke1 keeps running along the first rank.
Ke3 follows, maintaining the pressure.
Kd1 avoids the renewed mating threat.
Kd3 follows along the third rank.
Kc1 continues toward the queenside.
Kxc3 removes the rear c-pawn. That change opens the future h8–a1 queen diagonal; the reverse walk is disclosed source context before the separate later node.
branches.explanation: Kxb3 removes the b-pawn. That change opens the future h8–a1 queen diagonal; the reverse walk is disclosed source context before the separate later node.

branches.title: Promote, deflect the rook and run back
commentary: Begin in the separately reconstructed late source diagram after the kings return to g1/g3. The c3 pawn has disappeared.
h8=Q creates a queen that guards a1 along h8–a1, so ...Ra1 would no longer mate.
Rxh8 removes that queen but pulls the rook from the a-file.
c7 uses the gained tempo to create a pawn one step from promotion.
Ra8 returns to the a-file and renews the mating threat.
Kf1 starts the king’s second run along the first rank.
Kf3 follows to recreate the mating threat.
Ke1 steps away again.
Ke3 follows along the third rank.
Kd1 continues the escape.
Kd3 keeps the opposition and threat.
Kc1 runs toward the queenside.
Kc3 follows but cannot give a rook check from the a-file without releasing the king.
Kb1 reaches the critical safe endpoint of this route.
Kb3 is the illustrated king approach, but it cannot renew the same mating net.
d7 creates connected seventh-rank passers. The exact position is winning: each pawn guards the other’s promotion square. Further conversion is not asserted to be an immediate mate.
branches.explanation: d7 creates connected seventh-rank passers. The exact position is winning: each pawn guards the other’s promotion square. Further conversion is not asserted to be an immediate mate.

branches.title: Push the h-pawn before arranging c5
commentary: Compare the source’s premature pawn race without first gaining the c5 tempo.
h7 gives away the forced win, but the exact position is still drawn against best play.
Rf8 stops the h-pawn and keeps the king confined.
d7 is the losing error in this selected comparison: it leaves both promotion threats stopped while Black’s king can approach.
Kg4 begins Black’s king approach.
c5 tries to build the pawn chain too late.
Kf5 walks toward the central passers.
c6 tries to support promotion.
Ke6 reaches the d-pawn.
c7 advances again, but the d-pawn can be captured.
Kxd7 removes the advanced d-pawn. Black retains a checked win; White has not made a successful promotion race.
branches.explanation: Kxd7 removes the advanced d-pawn. Black retains a checked win; White has not made a successful promotion race.

exercises.prompt: Why does losing the c3 pawn help White’s promotion idea?
exercises.answer: It opens h8–g7–f6–e5–d4–c3–b2–a1. A queen on h8 can now answer ...Ra1, forcing the rook to spend a tempo capturing it.

startContext: Begin at the complete seven-piece source root. The first king walk is checked through ...Kxc3. A separately reconstructed late diagram after the reverse walk checks the queen deflection and second run. The omitted return is source context, not an invented connecting line.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
sourceCorrections: The h7 comparison is drawn after ...Rf8; the selected d7 continuation then loses. The lesson distinguishes those exact outcomes instead of calling h7 itself a forced loss.
